options.title: One list, every room
options.line: Every room in one fixed order, each row saying whether it is free and until when, the way the wall chart does.

options.title: Free rooms first
options.line: Free rooms in a region of their own at the top, each with its own Book action; the busy rooms below.

options.title: The day as a grid
options.line: Every room against the hours of the day, with a line at now; what frees up next is on the same line.

gallery.title: From the fresh pass, as it came

items.title: A plan of the floor, free rooms lit
items.line: Made with no knowledge of today's screens; its structure is on the board too, under one of the letters.

seats.line: B fits a front desk: her question is what is free now, and B answers it before anything else.
All three show only what the product holds: room status, when a booking ends and when the next one starts.
At 390 px the hours of C scroll sideways and the line at now leaves the screen.
Asked whether anything is free right now, the reader answered fastest on B, then on A, and slowest on C.

recommendation.reason: It answers her one question, what is free right now, before anything else, and puts a walk-in two clicks from the screen.

question: Which structure goes on to Detail: A, B or C?
